Now you try. What is 52 times 100? How many places does each digit move? Fill the empty places with 0.
Now you try. A game has 5 packs. Each pack has 30 cards. How many cards are there in all? Think of 30 as tens. Multiply the tens.
Now you try. 90 stickers come on sheets of 10. Share them fairly among 3 friends. How many stickers does each friend get? Count the tens. Share the tens.
Now you try. You have 23 stickers. Each page holds 4. How many pages can you fill all the way? Make groups of 4 until you cannot make another.
Now you try. A floor is 23 feet long and 4 feet wide. Break 23 into 20 and 3. How many square feet is the floor? Multiply each part by 4. Then add the parts.
Now you try. A train has 4 cars. Each car has 253 seats. How many seats are on the train? Multiply each part by 4. Then add all three parts.
Now you try. A store has 4 boxes. Each box holds 127 crayons. Multiply the standard way. How many crayons are there? Start with the ones. Multiply, then add any carry.
Now you try. A garden is 23 feet long and 15 feet wide. How many square feet is the garden? Find all four pieces. Then add them.
Now you try. A rug covers 96 square feet. It is 3 feet wide. Break 96 into 90 and 6. How long is the rug? Share each part by 3. Then add the answers.
Now you try. Find 384 divided by 3. Start with the hundreds. Divide, multiply, take away, bring down.
Now you try. 30 children are going to the zoo. Each van holds 4 children. How many vans do they need? Divide. Then read the question to decide what the leftover means.
Now you try. A shop has 4 boxes of pencils. Each box holds 25 pencils. The shop sells 47 pencils. How many pencils are left? Find the hidden number first. Then answer the question.

Now you try. Cut every piece of one half into smaller pieces so there are 6 in all. one half equals how many sixths? What is the missing top number? Find what the bottom was multiplied by. Multiply the top by the same number.
Now you try. Compare five eighths and two sixths. Which sign goes in the middle? five eighths ? two sixths Check each fraction against half. Is it above half or below half?
Now you try. Compare three fourths and seven eighths. Which sign goes in the middle? three fourths ? seven eighths Make the pieces the same size first. Then compare the tops.
Now you try. Break five eighths apart. five eighths equals one eighth plus ? What fraction is missing? Count the pieces in the whole fraction. Find how many pieces are still missing.
Now you try. What is one sixth plus four sixths? The pieces are the same size. Add the pieces and keep the bottom number.
Now you try. What is seven eighths minus two eighths? The pieces are the same size. Take away pieces and keep the bottom number.
Now you try. Write 2 and one fourth as fourths. 2 and one fourth equals how many fourths? What is the missing top number? Count the fourths in the wholes. Then add the extra fourth.
Now you try. What is 2 and one fourth plus 1 and two fourths? Add the wholes. Add the pieces. Then put them together.
Now you try. What is 4 times one fifth? Count the copies of the piece. Keep the piece size.
Now you try. Look at the ends. What is this? Look at both ends. A dot stops. An arrow keeps going.
Now you try. Is this angle acute, right or obtuse? Picture a square corner at the point. Is the angle narrower, the same or wider?
Now you try. The angle is drawn on a protractor. How many degrees is it? Start at the 0 on the bottom ray. Count up to the other ray.
Now you try. The whole angle is a right angle, 90 degrees. One part is 30 degrees. How many degrees is the other part? The parts add up to the whole. Take away the part you know.
Now you try. Are these lines parallel, perpendicular or neither? Do the lines meet? If they cross, is it at a square corner?
Now you try. Look at the angles. Is this an acute triangle, a right triangle or an obtuse triangle? Find the biggest angle. Compare it with a right angle.
Now you try. Which name fits this shape best? Count the pairs of parallel sides. Then check the corners and the sides.
Now you try. Fold along the dashed line. Do the two halves match exactly? Picture folding along the dashed line. Does every part land on a matching part?
Now you try. A bar is cut into 10 equal strips. You have zero point four of the bar. Write it as a fraction. The number after the point tells how many strips. The bar has 10 strips.
Now you try. This grid has 100 equal squares. What part is shaded, as a decimal? Count the shaded squares. Then write the hundredths after the point.
Now you try. You shade zero point seven of a 100-square grid. How many small squares do you shade? Each tenth is one full column. Count the squares in those columns.
Now you try. What number is at the dot? Find what one jump is worth. Then count the jumps from 0.
Now you try. Which sign goes between zero point six and zero point five eight? Look at the tenths first.
Now you try. Add. two tenths plus five hundredths equals what? Change the tenths into hundredths. Then add.
Now you try. You have 4 dollars, 1 dime and 7 pennies. How much money is that? Dollars, then the point, then dimes, then pennies.
Now you try. In 70, the 7 is in the tens place. What is the 7 worth if it slides one place to the left? Find the place one step to the left. It's worth 10 times as much.
Now you try. Multiply. 45 times 1,000 equals what? Count the zeros. Slide every digit that many places.
Now you try. Write 10 to the fourth as a number. Count how many tens to multiply. Each one adds a zero.
Now you try. Round each number to its biggest place, then multiply. About how much is 32 times 589? Round both numbers first. Then use a fact and write the zeros.
Now you try. How many meters is 8 kilometers? Is the new unit smaller or bigger? Smaller, multiply. Bigger, divide.
Now you try. A jug holds 3 liters of juice. Each cup holds 250 milliliters. How many cups can you fill? Change the liters to milliliters first. Then find how many cups.
Now you try. A farmer plants 7 rows of corn. Each row has 128 corn plants. How many corn plants are in the field? Multiply each part by 7. Then add all the parts.
Now you try. A bookshop gets 24 boxes. Each box holds 115 books. How many books does the shop get? Multiply 115 by 20 and by 4. Then add the two answers.
Now you try. Multiply the standard way. 142 times 23 equals what? Make a row for the ones and a row for the tens. Then add the two rows.
Now you try. Multiply the standard way. 214 times 123 equals what? Make one row for each digit of 123. Start each new row with one more 0.
Now you try. Estimate 406 times 27 first. Then multiply the standard way to find the exact answer. Estimate first. Then multiply, and check that your answer is close to the estimate.
Now you try. 420 students ride buses that each seat 60 students. How many buses do they fill? Think of both numbers in tens. Then use a fact you know.
Now you try. 85 kids come to the field. The coach puts 17 kids on each team. How many teams can she make? Round 17 to the nearest ten and guess. Then multiply to check.
Now you try. The shop has 161 roses. It puts 23 roses in each bunch. How many bunches can it make? Guess with round numbers. If the guess is too big, try one less.
Now you try. The store gets 325 eggs. Each carton holds 13 eggs. How many cartons can it fill? Divide the tens first. Then bring down the ones and divide again.
Now you try. 24 kids share 1,128 stickers equally. How many stickers does each kid get? Find where to start. Then bring down one digit at a time.
Now you try. A fruit stand packs 3 bags. Each bag has 4 apples and 5 pears. Which number sentence shows all the fruit? Keep one bag together inside the parentheses. Then show how many bags.

Now you try. The board shows 4 times 6 plus 5, all together. A class makes this story, 4 bags, each with 6 red marbles and 5 green marbles. How many marbles are in the story? Do the part in the parentheses first. Then do the rest of the story.

Now you try. A school buys 24 boxes of markers. Each box has 36 markers. The markers are shared equally among 27 classes. How many markers does each class get? Find the hidden number first. Then use it to answer the question.

Now you try. A movie theater has 32 rows of seats. Each row has 25 seats. For the late show, 247 tickets are sold. How many seats are still empty? Use the tape. Solve one part at a time, then check what the question asks.
Now you try. Add. one third plus one sixth equals what? Make the pieces the same size first. Then add.
Now you try. What is the smallest piece size that one half and one fifth can both be cut into? Type the new bottom number. Count by each bottom number. Find the first number in both lists.
Now you try. Take away. five sixths minus one third equals what? Make the pieces the same size first. Then take away.
Now you try. Add. 1 and one half plus 2 and three fourths equals what? Add the wholes. Then make the pieces match and add them.
Now you try. Take away. 4 and one third minus 1 and two thirds equals what? Not enough pieces? Break 1 whole first.
Now you try. Is five eighths plus two thirds more or less than 1? Compare each fraction to one half.
Now you try. Kim reads for two thirds hour. Tom reads for one sixth hour. How much longer does Kim read? Draw it. Then decide, put together, or find the gap.

Now you try. The chart shows how far 7 snails crawled, in feet. How much farther did the snail that went farthest crawl than the one that went shortest? Read the numbers under the X marks. Then take away.
Now you try. 2 pizzas are shared equally by 3 friends. How much pizza does each friend get? Cut every pizza so each friend gets a slice. Then count one friend’s slices.
Now you try. What is three fourths of 20? Cut into equal parts first. Then take the parts the top number asks for.

Now you try. You have half a pan. You eat one fourth of that half. How much of the whole pan is that? Find one fourth times one half. Take the piece of the half. Then count how many pieces like it fill the whole pan.
Now you try. A mat is one half meter wide and two thirds meter long. What is its area, in square meters? Cut one square meter to match the sides. Count the pieces the mat covers.
Now you try. Without working it out, is two thirds times 9 bigger than 9, smaller than 9, or equal to 9? Is the fraction more than 1, less than 1, or exactly 1?
Now you try. You have 3 yards of ribbon. Each bow uses one half yard. How many bows can you make? Find 3 divided by one half. Cut every yard into pieces the size of one bow. Count all the pieces.

Now you try. one fourth of a pie is left. 2 friends share it equally. How much of the whole pie does each friend get? Find one fourth divided by 2. Cut the shaded piece for the friends. Then count pieces that size in the whole pie.
Now you try. A rope is 6 feet long. You cut it into pieces that are each one third foot long. How many pieces do you get? Read what the story asks. Part of the rope, or how many pieces fit?
Now you try. Write 36 thousandths with a point. Thousandths go in the third place after the point.
Now you try. Which sign goes between them? Zero point seven, and zero point six nine eight. Line up the places. Find the first place that is different.
Now you try. Round five point six four to the nearest tenth. Find the two tenths it sits between. Pick the closer one.
Now you try. Add. Twenty-three point five six plus four point eight equals what? Line up the points. Add from the right. Bring the point down.
Now you try. Take away. Six point four minus two point seven five equals what? Put a zero in the empty place. Then take away from the right.
Now you try. Multiply. 4 times one and thirty-two hundredths equals what? Break the decimal into parts. Multiply each part. Then add.
Now you try. Multiply. Four point five seven times 100 equals what? Count the zeros in 100. Move every digit that many places.
Now you try. Divide. Seven and five tenths divided by 3 equals what? Count the decimal in tenths. Share them. Then write it with a point.
Now you try. How many meters is four point two kilometers? Smaller unit, multiply. Bigger unit, divide.
Now you try. Each small cube is the same size. How many cubes fill this box? Count every cube once, even the hidden ones.
Now you try. A box is 5 cubes long, 2 cubes wide and 3 layers high. How many cubes fill it? Find one layer. Then multiply by the number of layers.
Now you try. A box is 4 centimeters long, 3 centimeters wide and 5 centimeters tall. What is its volume in cubic centimeters? Multiply the length by the width. Then multiply by the height.

Now you try. Two boxes are joined. Box A is 5 centimeters long, 3 centimeters wide and 2 centimeters tall. Box B is 2 centimeters long, 3 centimeters wide and 4 centimeters tall. What is the total volume in cubic centimeters? Find the volume of each box. Then add the two.

Now you try. A mat is 1 and one half feet long and 1 and one half feet wide. Each small tile is one half foot on a side. How many square feet is the mat? Count the small tiles. Then change them to square feet.
Now you try. Is every rectangle a parallelogram? Think of the rule for the family. Does the shape follow it?
Now you try. Each cube is 1 cubic inch. What is the volume of this box in cubic inches? Count the cubes one layer at a time. Each cube is 1 cubic inch.
Now you try. How far across is point A? Go along the bottom first, until you are right under the point.
Now you try. Which point is at 3, 1? Go across first, then up. Which point is there?
Now you try. Pattern A, start at 0, add 2. Pattern B, start at 0, add 8. What is the 5th number in pattern B? Start at 0. Follow the rule one step at a time.
Now you try. Pattern A, start at 0, add 1. Pattern B, start at 0, add 3. Pattern A goes across. When the dot is 2 across, how far up is it? Find the column. The bottom number tells how far up.
Now you try. Point A is at 1 comma 4. Point B is at 8 comma 4. How many units apart are they? Find the number they share. Subtract the other two.
Now you try. On the map, the school is at 2 comma 3 and the pool is at 2 comma 9. How many blocks apart are they? Find the number they share. Subtract the other two.
Now you try. A bracelet pattern has 4 green beads for every 3 yellow beads. Green beads are 4 out of every how many beads? The whole means every bead in one set, both colors.
Now you try. A lemonade recipe uses 2 lemons for every 5 cups of water. How many cups of water go with 6 lemons? Find what the lemons were multiplied by. Do the same to the water.
Now you try. A pack of 4 pens costs 7 dollars. How much does one pen cost? Split the total into one equal part for each pen.
Now you try. 4 movie tickets cost 18 dollars. How much do 6 tickets cost? Find the price of one ticket first. Then multiply.
Now you try. A smoothie uses 2 cups of berries for every 3 cups of yogurt. How many cups of yogurt go with 10 cups of berries? Use the columns you already have. Multiply one, or add two together.
Now you try. A club has 3 boys for every 4 girls. There are 28 members. How many girls are in the club? Count all the boxes first. Then find what one box holds.
Now you try. A rug is 5 yards long. 1 yard is 3 feet. How many feet long is the rug? Start from one yard. Smaller units means more of them.
Now you try. A train goes 150 miles in 3 hours. How many miles does it go in one hour? Cut the trip into one equal jump for each hour.

Now you try. You have two thirds of a pan of cornbread. Each serving is one sixth of the pan. How many servings can you cut? Find two thirds divided by one sixth. Cut the shaded part into pieces the size of one serving. Then count them.

Now you try. You have 3 liters of juice. Each bottle holds three fourths liter. How many bottles can you fill? Find 3 divided by three fourths. Keep the first number, change divide to times, and flip the fraction you divide by.
Now you try. Find 1 and one half times 2 and one third. Change both mixed numbers into fractions. Then multiply.
Now you try. You have 3 and three fourths pounds of ground beef. Each patty uses three fourths pound. How many patties can you make? Change the mixed number into a fraction. Then flip and multiply.
Now you try. You have 4 yards of ribbon. Each bow uses two thirds yard. How many bows can you make? Start with the amount you have. Divide by the size of one bow.
Now you try. What is the biggest number that is a factor of both 16 and 24? List the factors of each number. Find the biggest one on both lists.
Now you try. What is the smallest number that is a multiple of both 6 and 8? Count by each number. Stop at the first number both counts reach.
Now you try. Take away. Fifteen point four minus six point two three seven equals what? Line up the points. Fill the empty places with zeros. Take away from the right.
Now you try. Multiply. Three point two times one point four equals what? Multiply without the points. Count the places. Put the point back.
Now you try. Divide. Nine point four five divided by 3 equals what? Put the point on top first. Then divide like whole numbers.
Now you try. Divide. Seven point two divided by zero point three equals what? Multiply both numbers by 10 or 100 until the outside number is whole. Then divide.
Now you try. Find 4,368 divided by 24. Guess each digit with a round number. Multiply, take away, bring down.
Now you try. Pens come 3 for 2 dollars and 85 cents or 5 for 4 dollars and 60 cents. Which is the better buy? Find the price of one pen in each pack. Pick the lower one.
Now you try. This grid has 100 equal squares. What percent of the grid is shaded? Count the shaded squares. Out of 100, that count is the percent.
Now you try. What percent is one fourth? Make the fraction out of 100. Then read the percent.
Now you try. What is 40 percent of 70? Find 10 percent first. Then take the parts you need.
Now you try. 12 is 25 percent of what number? Find how many equal pieces make 100 percent. Then count them all.
Now you try. Shoes cost 60 dollars. They are 20 percent off. What is the sale price, in dollars? Find the money you save. Then take it away from the price.
Now you try. A jacket costs 50 dollars. The sales tax is 6 percent. What is the total, in dollars? Find the tax. Then add it to the price.

Now you try. You put 600 dollars in a bank that pays 3 percent a year. How many dollars does the bank pay you in 2 years? Just what the bank pays, not the 600 dollars. Find one year first. Then multiply by the years.
Now you try. A box holds n pencils. You also have 4 more pencils, so you have n plus 4 pencils. How many pencils is that when n equals 6? Find what n stands for. Put that number where the n is.
Now you try. Which shows 7 more than n? Find the action word. Then write it with n.
Now you try. What is 2 n plus 5 when n equals 6? Put the number where the letter is. Then do the math.
Now you try. What is 3 cubed? Write the big number as many times as the small number says. Then multiply.
Now you try. What is 5 plus 2 times 3 squared? Parentheses, then exponents, then times and divide, then plus and minus.
Now you try. Which is the same as 4 times x plus 3, all together? Multiply the number outside by every part inside.
Now you try. Solve x plus 6 equals 15. What is x? Take the same amount off both sides until x is alone.
Now you try. Solve 4 x equals 28. What is x? Divide both sides by the number in front of x.
Now you try. Which number line shows x is less than 6? Decide the dot first, does the number itself work? Then decide which way the arrow goes.

Now you try. This shape has a base of 7 centimeters and a height of 4 centimeters. Its slanted side is 5 centimeters. What is its area in square centimeters? Multiply the base by the straight-up height.
Now you try. A triangle has a base of 8 centimeters and a height of 5 centimeters. What is its area in square centimeters? Multiply the base by the height. Then take half.

Now you try. A wall is a rectangle 8 feet wide and 5 feet tall with a triangle roof 3 feet tall on top. What is its area in square feet? Cut it into a rectangle and a triangle. Find each area, then add.

Now you try. This box is 5 centimeters long, 3 centimeters wide and 2 centimeters tall. It is unfolded flat below. How many square centimeters of paper cover it? Find the area of every flat side, then add all six.
Now you try. A box is 3 and one half ft long, 2 feet wide and 1 and one half ft tall. What is its volume in cubic feet? Change the mixed numbers to fractions. Then multiply all three edges.
Now you try. Two angles sit side by side on a straight line. One is 65 degrees. How many degrees is the other? The angles on a straight line add up to 180 degrees. Take away the one you know.
Now you try. Four towers have 3, 7, 4 and 6 cubes. If the cubes are shared fairly, how many cubes are in each tower? Add all the cubes. Then share the total into equal towers.
Now you try. Five seedlings are 8, 2, 5, 9 and 4 inches tall. What is the middle height? Sort the heights first. Then find the one in the middle.
Now you try. 12 kids said how many brothers and sisters they have. Which number is the most common? Find the tallest stack. Read the number under it.
Now you try. Leo scored 6, 13, 8, 17 and 10 points in five games. What is the biggest score minus the smallest score? Find the smallest and the biggest. Then subtract.
Now you try. Five kids get 6 dollars, 5 dollars, 7 dollars, 6 dollars and 36 dollars a week. Which middle describes these amounts best? Look for a number far from the rest.
Now you try. Kids marked how many books they read this month. How many kids read 3 or more books? Find the stacks you need. Count their Xs and add.
Now you try. This spinner has 8 equal parts. What is the chance of landing on blue? Ways it can happen on top. All the ways on the bottom.
Now you try. A bag has 5 marbles, 1 yellow and 4 purple. You pick one without looking. How likely is yellow? Find the chance as a fraction. Then see where it sits on the line.
How many plates are there? How many cookies are on each plate?
There are 3 groups of 5. Count by 5s, one plate at a time. 5, 10, and keep going.
How many groups are there? How many are in each group?

Find the area of each piece. Then add the two areas.

Are all the pieces the same size?
Compare the middle piece with the pieces at the ends.

Put your finger on each piece and compare it with the next one.
How many equal pieces is the whole bar cut into?
The shaded piece is 1 of those pieces. Put the 1 on top.
How many equal pieces is the strip cut into?
You ate 1 piece. That number goes on top.

How many equal pieces is the whole pan cut into?
Count only the shaded pieces. That number goes on top.

Start at 0 and count the jumps until you reach the dot.
Start at 0. Count the jumps to the dot. The 0 is where you start, not a jump.

Each piece on the top bar was cut into 2 smaller pieces. Did the shaded amount change?
Each piece on the top bar sits over how many small pieces below?
Look under the shaded piece on top. Count the small pieces under it.

Count the shaded pieces. Are any pieces white?
